forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred west of TAS will continue to drift eastwards, while a weak low pressure system and trough near the western border continue to move eastwards. The high will drift southeast of Tasmania by Monday, while the trough and low continue to move eastwards across SA, clearing to the east later Tuesday. Another high will develop south of the state on Wednesday. Another trough extends into the far west of SA later Thursday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible showers or thunderstorms about the north, west and Eyre Peninsula, extending eastwards over the northeast and central parts. Maximum temperatures generally above average, tending below average about the far southwest and adjacent to the NSW border. East to northeasterly winds, freshening about western and central parts, ahead of a fresh southwest to southerly change moving across western parts during the day.

Possible showers or thunderstorms in the west, more likely west of about Ceduna during the afternoon, possibly extending over Eyre Peninsula during the late afternoon or evening. Moderate to fresh southeast to northeasterly winds, shifting southwest to southeasterly in the far west later.

Possible showers or thunderstorms about the north and east. Maximum temperatures above average in the east, grading to below average in the west. Moderate to fresh northeast to northwesterly winds about eastern parts at first, with fresh southwest to southeasterly winds in the west. extending throughout during the day.

Possible showers or thunderstorms about the west and far north. Maximum temperatures above average in the northeast, grading to below average elsewhere. Southwest to southeasterly winds, fresh at times near the coast.

text.p: Possible showers or thunderstorms about the west and far north, becoming more likely in the far west. Maximum temperatures generally above average, grading to below average about the southern agricultural area and in the northwest. Generally southeast to northeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: Broadly less than 2 mm across the state. Falls increasing to 2 to 5 mm about the west, north and parts of the agricultural area, with higher falls of 5 to 15 mm about the west and far north and isolated higher falls of 10 to 20 mm with thunderstorms.
